# Evaluating $\int_{0}^{0.1} \cos(100x^2)\,dx$ with Accuracy $\alpha = 0.001$

## Strategy: Taylor Series Expansion

I expand $\cos(100x^2)$ about $x = 0$:

$$\cos(100x^2) = 1 - \frac{(100x^2)^2}{2!} + \frac{(100x^2)^4}{4!} - \frac{(100x^2)^6}{6!} + \cdots$$

$$= 1 - 5000\,x^4 + \frac{10^8}{24}\,x^8 - \frac{10^{12}}{720}\,x^{12} + \cdots$$

## Term-by-Term Integration on $[0,\, 0.1]$

| Term | Integral | Value |
|------|----------|-------|
| $\displaystyle\int_0^{0.1} 1\,dx$ | $0.1$ | $0.100000$ |
| $\displaystyle\int_0^{0.1} -5000\,x^4\,dx = -1000\cdot(0.1)^5$ | | $-0.010000$ |
| $\displaystyle\int_0^{0.1} \frac{10^8}{24}x^8\,dx = \frac{10^8}{216}(0.1)^9 = \frac{1}{2160}$ | | $+0.000463$ |
| $\displaystyle\int_0^{0.1} -\frac{10^{12}}{720}x^{12}\,dx = -\frac{10^{12}}{9360}(0.1)^{13} = -\frac{1}{93600}$ | | $-0.000011$ |

The next (fifth) term has magnitude $\sim 10^{-7}$, far below the required tolerance.

## Summing

$$\int_0^{0.1}\cos(100x^2)\,dx \approx 0.1 - 0.01 + 0.000463 - 0.000011 = 0.090452$$

## Accuracy Check

The remainder after the fourth retained term is bounded by the magnitude of the fifth term:

$$R \lesssim \frac{10^{16}}{5040}\cdot\frac{(0.1)^{17}}{17} \approx 1.2\times 10^{-7} \ll 0.001$$

So the result is accurate well within $\alpha = 0.001$.

## Result

Rounding to the required precision:

$$\boxed{0.090}$$
